exposure: Neurostimulation (spinal cord stimulation) for chronic low back pain
cohort: A 37-year-old woman with severe chronic low back pain unresponsive to pharmacologic treatments, who received neurostimulation before pregnancy, ceased it during pregnancy, and delivered a baby.
finding: Neurostimulation before pregnancy for chronic low back pain, followed by cessation during pregnancy, resulted in excellent maternal pain control and quality of life, a complication-free pregnancy, and a healthy baby, suggesting a risk-free management approach for both patient and child.
followup_time: Up to the end of pregnancy and immediate post-birth period for neurostimulator reactivation
